articles.title: Public media freedom has been eroded across central Europe. Now Czechs are rallying to protect theirs
articles.description: Huge protest planned in Prague to oppose government’s plan to scrap licence fee, which critics say could give ministers more leverage over newsrooms Daniel Stach was an erstwhile junior international slalom kayaker when he first walked into the headquarters of Czech Television in 2010. He had answered a Facebook ad inviting viewers to a behind-the-scenes tour of his favourite programme, a current affairs show called Hyde Park CT24. He did not expect to be offered a job shortly afterwards. Stach, now 38, presents a science offshoot of that show doing long-form interviews. But he has also emerged as one of the most recognised public faces of the campaign to save the mandatory licence fees that fund the nation’s public broadcasters. Continue reading...

articles.title: Barbara Kingsolver: ‘What does love feel like? At 16, breaking the speed limit. Years later, a warm bath’
articles.description: The author on the FBI tapping her phone, teaching herself to read aged three, and why she knits in meetings Born in Maryland, in the US, Barbara Kingsolver, 71, won a music scholarship to DePauw University in Indiana. She became a journalist and published her first novel, The Bean Trees, in 1988. Her award-winning books include The Poisonwood Bible, The Lacuna and Demon Copperhead, which was published in 2022 and won the Pulitzer, the James Tait Black prize and the Women’s prize for fiction. In 2025, she founded the Higher Ground Women’s Recovery Residence in Lee County, Virginia, where the novel is set. Her latest novel is Partita . She lives in Virginia with her second husband and has two children. When were you happiest? Right after the births of my children. Those hormones are strong medicine: they erase all memory of recent gruelling events and crown you goddess, author of divine creation. Continue reading...

articles.title: King Æthelstan founded England in the year 927. Why don’t we celebrate that anniversary? | Tom Holland
articles.description: Nearly 1,100 years ago, the nation’s first king drove out the ‘heathen’ Vikings, declared war on starvation and made ‘Englalonde’ what it is today On 4 July, the United States celebrated its 250th birthday with all the razzmatazz and dazzle characteristic of an American public occasion. Next summer, on 12 July, England will be celebrating the 1,100th anniversary of the event that, more than any other, marked the founding of the country – but of razzmatazz and dazzle there will be, I suspect, very little. The great turning point took place on 12 July 927, beside the river Eamont in what today is Cumbria. Here, amid an untamed wilderness of mountains and lakes, the most powerful king in Britain had summoned other kings and lords from across the island to meet him for a summit. Continue reading...

articles.title: Guardian to follow lives of eight young people in their search for work
articles.description: How long will it take? What challenges will they face? Series to shine light on one of biggest crises facing UK ‘The social contract is broken’: young people on feeling shut out of careers Britain is at risk of creating a lost generation. Across the country, almost a million young people – one in eight – are struggling to make the leap from school to the world of work on a lasting basis. articles.title: ‘I relive that mission every single day of my life’: how Black soldiers handled the Vietnam war
articles.description: In ambitious documentary Soul Patrol, the complicated experiences of the Vietnam war’s first Black special ops team are explored both on and off the battleground Ask the average American to name an elite US fighting force, and they might kick off with the Rangers or the Seals. But during the Vietnam war, a specialized patrol of army volunteers became critical to the US military effort. Known as long-range reconnaissance patrols, or LRRPs, these small teams of six to eight soldiers were dropped behind enemy lines to track supply routes and hostile positions, sometimes for days at a time. Stealth was essential. Their job was to identify targets and call in the cavalry, usually in the form of airstrikes, while avoiding direct engagement with enemy forces to preserve their cover. articles.description: Essential Water Infrastructure Improvement Work gets underway – Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen NI Water is set to commence an upgrade of the water infrastructure on Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen in early August for approximately 6 weeks. The work will see around 400m of new watermain being laid along Cornagrade Road, starting at Cherrymount Roundabout on Monday 3 rd August and progressing as far as the second entrance to Kilmacormick Road. To facilitate the laying of this new watermain, a lane closure will be in place around each working area and signage will be in place. Working areas will be kept as short as possible (around 100m) with temporary traffic lights in place to manage the flow of traffic. Access to residential and business properties on and adjacent to Cornagrade Road will be available at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be affected for a short period of time while the pipelaying passes. Any bus stop located within a working area will be temporarily relocated.

articles.title: Derry - NIW Scheme - Racecourse Rd - from 27 July
articles.description: Essential water network upgrade to get underway on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett NI Water is set to begin an essential watermain upgrade on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett (Derry/Londonderry) on Monday 27 th July to improve the resilience of the local water supply network. The work, which involves laying around 170 metres of new watermain between Carnhill Roundabout and Greenhaw Road, will replace a section of the 50-year-old Ballyarnett Water Trunkmain which has been prone to bursts. The upgrade will help to protect homes from flooding, should a burst occur in the future, and provide improved access for NI Water maintenance. A l ane closure controlled by temporary traffic lights will be in place on Racecourse Road around the working area from Monday 27 th July for four weeks. A further two weeks of work will take place in the adjacent verge which will not require any traffic management. Temporary traffic lights will be manned during peak hours and access to properties will be maintained at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be temporarily unavailable. Once the lane closure is removed, works will move into the adjacent verge to complete the final phase of w

articles.title: Craigavon - Closure of Maple Path & Parkmore Footbridges
articles.description: Closure of Maple Path and Parkmore Footbridges, Craigavon The Department for Infrastructure have announced that the Maple Path and Parkmore footbridges in Craigavon will be closed from Thursday 4 June 2026. Detailed engineering inspections identified structural concerns, and it has been concluded that the closure of these footbridges is necessary while a permanent solution is developed. Alternative local walking routes are available and will be signposted where appropriate. While these routes may increase journey times for some users, they will provide access around the affected areas. The Department recognises the importance of both footbridges to local residents and apologises for any inconvenience caused. However, as the Department’s infrastructure assets age there will always be an eventual need to replace structures that present safety issues or have come to the end of their natural lifespan. Further information on future proposals for the bridges will be provided as work progresses. The Department would like to thank the public for their patience and cooperation.

articles.description: For a drama that is meant to explore female trauma, Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy are given very little to do as small-town lawyers. They sure don’t make his laaahf easy! articles.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: a lotion to cure autumn dryness – and relieve eczema sufferers’ sore skin
articles.description: Bioderma’s new eczema lotion will be comforting for anyone with dry skin. Plus another brilliant problem solving mosituriser I spent much of my childhood basted in crude, heavy-duty emollient creams and grim bath oils. But few patients are as short-changed as eczema sufferers, whose treatments and regimens are not only joyless, but sometimes provide little reward for the trouble. Although unctuous emollients are necessary to protect a compromised skin barrier, they have a habit of just “sitting” there greasily, refusing to sink in or curtail the itch. The French pharmaceutical brand Bioderma is finally advancing the conversation. Its extensive research into eczema, as well as a recent study of 500 sufferers (about one in five children and one in 10 adults struggle with the condition), were presented as a breakthrough in eczema care at last month’s EADV (European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology) conference in Vienna. articles.title: Country diary: An ancient bridge, laid low by one storm after another | Sara Hudston
articles.description: Exmoor, Somerset: Tarr Steps is no stranger to flooding, but the damage is becoming more and more frequent Fog cloaked the combe as we walked down to the River Barle, and for the first time in months I wished I were wearing gloves. A red kite wheeled overhead, the dull copper colour of its underparts matching the autumn leaves still clinging to the oaks. Red kites are still fairly uncommon on Exmoor, though their numbers have increased recently as the species pushes west. Several pheasants whirred past, calling loudly in alarm: they are also more numerous now, due to the spread of game-shooting estates. We were heading for Tarr Steps, the longest clapper bridge in Britain, an ancient footbridge nearly 55 metres long, with 17 arches braced across the Barle. It is constructed of pillars of piled rock set about two metres apart, spanned by huge, flat gritstones weighing up to two tonnes each. The whole edifice is held together by bulk and weight, without the aid of mortar, cement or ironwork. Its exact age is uncertain, but the existing structure is considered to be a medieval improvement of a simpler bronze age crossing. Continue reading...

articles.title: School-night wine - the best bottles for an impromptu midweek treat

We ate this gloriously garlicky, vinegar-spiked number with pasta, and it was a revelation. After one bite, it felt rude not to have some wine with it and, before I knew it, I had a glass of red in front of me. Today, I am championing school-night wine. Not because I want to be a bad influence, but because, in this restrained, over-scheduled, all-or-nothing age, we risk losing the impromptu pleasure of a nice drop – with food, say, or with a friend who has popped by, or just to offset the nervous strain of the children’s bedtime. articles.title: Does M John Harrison’s Booker win mean science fiction is finally accepted by a ‘snobby’ literary establishment?
articles.description: Kazuo Ishiguro, Jeff VanderMeer, Olivia Laing and other writers weigh in on the publishing world’s genre wars As M John Harrison was announced as the Booker prize winner on Monday evening, the 81-year-old looked gobsmacked. Decades into his career, and long overlooked by the mainstream literary establishment, he had just won a prize that has never before rewarded a writer known for science fiction, with a decidedly fantastical book. His fans, many leading authors among them, are thrilled. “For decades it was a standard – and correct – nerd whine to point out that sentence for sentence, book for book, Harrison was one of the greatest writers out there, full stop, but that ‘mainstream’ prizes never reflected that,” says China Miéville, who last week won the Goldsmiths prize with his 1,200-page speculative novel The Rouse . Back in 2002, Miéville wrote that Harrison not having won a Booker by that point proved “the bankruptcy and back-slapping generic snobbery of the literary establishment”. Now, he says: “I am so delighted, for Harrison, and for fiction.” Continue reading...

Cunk on Cinema is one such programme. The latest series from Diane Morgan’s sensationally idiotic documentarian is a three-part history of film that begins with our host reeling off some of humanity’s greatest achievements in her deadpan Bolton tones. Specifically, “conquering the landscape, growing the great wall of Chinese, discovering Mona Lisa and inventing global warming”. articles.title: Ofsted’s menacing inspections are still disastrous. Schools should answer to the communities they serve | Simon Jenkins
articles.description: For all the supposed improvements, inspectors still obsess over statistics and adjectives, but surely school success depends on teachers and parents The government regulation of state schools by Ofsted in England is a fiasco. Following the 2023 suicide of the Reading headteacher Ruth Perry, after her school was downgraded from outstanding to inadequate, Ofsted appears to have referred to a dictionary. Single words were replaced by colour-coded report cards , which use a wider range of different adjectives to grade abstractions such as personal development and wellbeing, achievement and leadership. Never has the concept of “education” seemed so empty. The reaction of the teaching profession to the new code has itself been devastating, as highlighted in a recent survey that showed more than half of headteachers in England polled after their schools were inspected under Ofsted’s new regime are now considering early retirement as a result of the experience. This sense of misery was also illustrated in a poll conducted by the National Education Union one year on from the introduction of the new framework, with 65% saying it is the same as or worse than before. But although she’s a dab hand at graceful, timeless presentation (and has a truly remarkable voice) Aalegra’s music has often struggled to match up to its aesthetic, hampered by her love of the greats and a penchant for broadly generic lyrics. Her most recent album, 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies , made some headway toward carving out a more distinctive sound, thanks to sparky and inventive production from Tyler, the Creator, No ID, P2J and the Neptunes, but still didn’t quite feel like the right fit. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League, it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique. As the WSL has grown in investment, profile and size, that narrative has started to shift a little. The investment gap is still large from the top to the bottom of the league. articles.title: No Retreat, No Add Vance
articles.description: No Retreat, No Add Vance By Michael Every of Rabobank It’s Friday the 13th, traditionally a day when bad things happen - so far we have bad omens; not just a spike in JGB and Australian bond yields this morning, but that Microsoft Outlook and Teams are both down, so I don’t know who will be able to read this. The US has decided it can’t reach a deal to end the Ukraine war without Europe, yet the Ukrainian press says, ‘Europe wants a seat at the table with Russia. It can't agree on who gets it.’ There seems little chance of any agreement being struck regardless of who gets that hot seat. Putin stated deploying foreign peacekeeping troops to Ukraine after a peace agreement is "absolutely unacceptable" and would be a continuation of war, implying risks of a military conflict with Moscow. Europe is preparing those peacekeepers now. Worse, Russia’s demands re: security architecture are obviously unacceptable to Europe. articles.title: Most Americans, Including Republicans, Want Congress To Pass Legislation To End Iran War; New Poll Finds
articles.description: Most Americans, Including Republicans, Want Congress To Pass Legislation To End Iran War; New Poll Finds Authored by Dave DeCamp via Antiwar.com , A new poll from Reuters/Ipsos has found that a majority of US adults, including the majority of Republicans, want Congress to pass legislation to end the Iran war , a conflict that's been extremely unpopular among the American people. The poll asked if respondents would support or oppose the incoming Democrat-led Congress passing legislation to end the Iran war, and 71%, including 51% of Republicans, said they would support the effort . The poll was conducted in the days following the midterm elections, which saw a major Republican defeat, and the war and the increase in the cost of living as a result of it were identified as the major factors in the Democrats' victory. Both Vice President JD Vance and President Trump have acknowledged that the war cost the GOP the midterms, though Trump continues to defend his decision to launch it and continues to escalate the ongoing blockade and sanctions campaign against the Islamic Republic . articles.description: Watch Live: Anthropic's Dario Amodei Joins JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon To Pitch Record IPO Anthropic is streaming a fireside chat today at 12 PM ET between CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon as part of the marketing push for what is shaping up to be one of the largest IPOs on record.  The Claude maker has set a $70–$78 price range for 825 million shares, implying a roughly $1 trillion valuation (closer to $1.4 trillion fully diluted) , with trading targeted for the Nasdaq under ticker ANT before Thanksgiving. JPMorgan is among the lead banks and is handling domestic retail marketing and allocations, with reports that a meaningful slice of the deal is being reserved for individual investors. The pairing is notable even by the standards of this cycle. Dimon has previously flagged how advanced models (including Anthropic’s own) have sharply raised cybersecurity risks, while JPMorgan is already a major Claude customer. articles.title: Dem Lawmakers Launch New Probe Of RFK Jr.
articles.description: Dem Lawmakers Launch New Probe Of RFK Jr. Authored by Zachary Stieber via The Epoch Times , Democratic lawmakers have begun new probes into Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., including whether he lied to Congress. One investigation looks into Kennedy's testimony during confirmation hearings in 2025 when he told senators that a trip he took to Samoa had "nothing to do with vaccines." Lawmakers cited recent media reports that showed Kennedy writing in 2019, the year of the trip, to the prime minister of Samoa, saying that deaths associated with the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine may have stemmed from the shot and proposing that his team conduct a "detailed health informatics assessment in Samoa of what happened with your MMR vaccines." While in Samoa, Kennedy met with activists who have spoken out against immunizations, according to the reports. "Evidence thus suggests that Kennedy's 2019 trip to Samoa was focused, in whole or in part, on vaccines," Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, and Sen. articles.title: British Universities Push Sharia Loans While Taxpayers Cover The Unpaid Tab
articles.description: British Universities Push Sharia Loans While Taxpayers Cover The Unpaid Tab Authored by Steve Watson via Modernity , British universities are now openly advertising government-backed "interest-free" student loans designed around Islamic finance rules. The Alternative Student Finance product, based on the principle of takaful, replaces interest with a mutual "contribution" that is ring-fenced to fund other students on the same scheme rather than flowing back into the Treasury. Official forecasts already expect nearly half of student debt never to be fully repaid, so British taxpayers will underwrite the shortfall while the ring-fenced pot serves a program primarily aimed at Muslim students , the Telegraph reports. British universities are preparing to offer interest-free sharia-compliant loans to Muslim students, with repayments used to fund others joining the scheme rather than going to the Treasury. The plans have sparked concerns that they could create a "two-tier system" in higher education. ? https://t.co/pB9wmbam8j — The Telegraph (@Telegraph) November 10, 2026 The scheme is open to anyone eligible for student finance, yet it exists because Islamic law prohibits interest. articles.title: After France, Belgium Is Europe's Next Debt Flashpoint
articles.description: After France, Belgium Is Europe's Next Debt Flashpoint Authored by Thomas Kolbe via American Thinker , In the shadow of France's sovereign debt crisis, other smoldering fires threaten to become a raging blaze. In Belgium, things could come to a flashpoint that sets the entire eurozone alight. Among the many catastrophic lessons of the great financial and sovereign debt crisis more than a decade ago, one came as a surprise: it is not the size of an economy that determines the outbreak of a sovereign debt crisis . It was tiny Greece, accounting for just 2.5 percent of the eurozone's total economic output, that came within a hair's breadth of blowing the union apart from within. At the time, Greece's sovereign debt reached 170 percent of GDP. Austerity was then the order of the day, and given the country's homogeneous population and undeniable state lethargy, it was ultimately accepted. But things hung by a thread. For in the eurozone, states are chained together through the bond market. The EU, and above all the eurozone, is simply not a federation like the United States. articles.title: United Airlines Moves To Ban Use Of AI Agents In Booking Flights For Customers
articles.description: United Airlines Moves To Ban Use Of AI Agents In Booking Flights For Customers Authored by Jacob Burg via The Epoch Times , United Airlines is moving to ban the use of artificial intelligence (AI) agents to make flight reservations on behalf of customers over concerns of possible security risks and violations of federal regulations. United warned travelers on Nov. 11 that sharing their account details with AI assistants could expose sensitive information and lead to "unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." For an AI agent to book a flight, a customer would have to give the model access to his or her personal account information, including payment credentials. Allowing an AI agent to complete a flight check-in may also violate Federal Aviation Administration and U.S. Department of Transportation regulations, the airline noted, because flight check-ins require a human acknowledgment that bags "do not contain banned substances like explosives." articles.description: Quality Over Quantity: The Missing Signal In Jobs Data That Explains The Vibecession Authored by Lance Roberts via RealInvestmentAdvice.com, Recession Indicators Turned Green. Job Quality Hasn’t. October’s jobs report pushed the headline recession indicators back to green, but “labor hoarding” explains why the earnings boom still isn’t reaching full-time workers. Key Takeaways S&P 500 earnings are on track to grow 31.4% in the third quarter, yet fewer Americans work full-time today than in September 2025. October payrolls beat every forecast at 165,000, but full-time employment, at 49.0% of the working-age population, remains well below its 2019 level of 50.6%. Companies are “hoarding” labor: output rose 3.7% last quarter while hours worked rose 0.1%, so productivity, not hiring, is carrying profits. Involuntary part-time work jumped 339,000 to 4.8 million in October, and pay growth of 3.1% still trails 3.7% inflation. The recession indicators flashing green – claims and layoffs – are the ones labor hoarding suppresses the longest. Here is the puzzle investors face right now. articles.title: Back To The Fax Machine: Microsoft's Meltdown Exposes The Agentic Economy's Weakest Link
articles.description: Back To The Fax Machine: Microsoft's Meltdown Exposes The Agentic Economy's Weakest Link Traders reached for fax machines, Japan's finance ministry pinned paper notices to the wall, and the AI assistants meant to automate the office went dark right along with the inbox. Hang in there clippy... For more than 18 hours, the AI agents Silicon Valley says will soon do your job couldn't read your email, because nobody could. A Microsoft 365 failure that began Thursday knocked out Outlook for businesses and governments in more than 70 countries and took Microsoft's own Copilot down with it , along with the Microsoft connectors that Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT use to reach users' mail and calendars. Every one of those failures has one thing in common: Exchange Online, Microsoft's cloud email and calendar backend. In its status notice Friday morning, Microsoft said features across its 365 services "that interact with Exchange Online and email services are impacted," while "elements of those services that do not depend on interaction with Exchange Online remain functional." articles.title: ICE Sets All-Time Records: 483,200 Deported, Arrests Nearly Double
articles.description: ICE Sets All-Time Records: 483,200 Deported, Arrests Nearly Double Authored by AG News Staff via American Greatness , U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested and deported more people over the last year than at any point in its 23-year history , the agency announced Thursday, according to an Associated Press report published by ABC News . ICE deported 483,200 people in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30. That was 9% more than the previous record of 442,640 set a year earlier, and 78 percent more than the 271,480 deported in 2024, the final year of Joe Biden's presidency. Arrests rose even faster. ICE made 474,850 arrests in the most recent 12-month period, roughly double the 239,890 from the year before and more than four times the 113,430 recorded in 2024. "Thanks to President Trump's leadership, ICE has been unleashed to target and remove illegal aliens so that we can save American lives," said Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. The agency made more than 48,000 arrests in September, following two straight months of record highs that peaked at 50,925 in August. articles.description: Soaring Electricity Costs Force Britain To Rethink Its Green Agenda Via City A.M., Labour is making affordable energy a central priority as high electricity prices undermine British industrial competitiveness. Decisions on North Sea drilling and electric vehicle targets are testing the government's commitment to net zero. Ministers face pressure to reform electricity levies while balancing economic growth against long-term climate goals. While it didn't make the headlines, Chancellor John Healey's Budget speech signaled a huge shift in positioning from previous governments over net zero . "Today I'm setting a new course on energy: to get UK energy costs down in line with Europe," Healey said. "From this point, our government priority is first and foremost cheaper energy, with clean power key to achieving this." The lines raised eyebrows in Westminster. articles.title: Helsinki Warns Ukraine Against Expanding War Into Gulf Of Finland After Russian Warship Struck
articles.description: Helsinki Warns Ukraine Against Expanding War Into Gulf Of Finland After Russian Warship Struck In a rare moment of the Ukraine war spilling far outside its boundaries into the north, Finland's military on Thursday alerted the world that its military detected a rare strike on a Russian navy vessel in the Baltic Sea. A spokesperson for the Finnish armed forces told Reuters they "detected… a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and has monitored the development of the situation ," but also noted somewhat ominously that Finland is not under "any immediate military threat." Illustrative, Reuters No other information was given to the mysterious alert, such as precise strike location and from where it originated, or exactly when it happeneed. Also, there's no information on casualties or damage.  Reuters has, however, noted that there's been an uptick in drone activity over the Baltic Sea region : Estonia, ⁠Latvia and Lithuania early on Wednesday issued warnings to citizens to take shelter due to drones in their airspace, and NATO scrambled warplanes ⁠in ​response.
